newsitem.title: USA: Baxter says U.S. renal prices stabilizing.
newsitem.headline: Baxter says U.S. renal prices stabilizing.

text.p: U.S. pricing levels are stabilizing in Baxter International Inc's key renal market, following 18 months of price-cutting by arch-rival Fresenius AG, said Baxter group vice president Donald Joseph.
Speaking on Tuesday at a meeting with reporters, Joseph said, "Pricing is starting to stabilize and we expect that to be that way going forward."
In July, Baxter said second-quarter growth in its renal business was held back by price competition from Fresenius.
Joseph said Baxter has had to lower its renal prices to keep up with Fresenius in the U.S. market.
"In Europe, for whatever reason, pricing has never been an issue. They have not taken prices down. We have not.... We've not been in a price competition at all in Europe," he said.
Deerfield, Illinois-based Baxter and Germany's Fresenius compete in Europe and the United States in the renal market for kidney dialysis products and services.
Fresenius recently acquired the large National Medical Care renal business of W.R. Grace & Co, beating out a rival offer for the former Grace unit made by Baxter.
Baxter's renal business generated 25 percent of total 1995 revenues. The company expects a similar ratio this year.

Renal care is Baxter's highest profit-margin areas and one of four principal business divisions that will constitute the new Baxter after its spin-off of Allegiance Corp, which takes away Baxter's lower-margin hospital supply and cost management services divisions.
